subject: Throughput & GPU pool sizing for Starlit AI — commit/discount discussion
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice@starlit-ai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@starlit-ai.com
Date: 2026-08-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing ask — production traffic profile + SLA goals

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We attached a short workload snapshot (starlit_workload_snapshot.csv) but wanted to call out the main points here so we can get a recommendation and a rough commit number from you: 

- Peak traffic: ~1,200 requests/minute (20 req/s) during peak windows (2 x 45-minute windows/day).
- Typical steady: ~400 requests/minute (6.7 req/s).
- Average input tokens: ~200 (users + system prompts).
- Average output tokens: ~250. 90th pct output can be ~600 tokens for long form generation.
- Context length: commonly 1k tokens, occasionally up to 4k for historical summaries.
- Concurrency pattern: many short-lived concurrent interactions (bursty), median request duration ~1.1s server-side.
- Requirement: 95th pct latency < 300ms for streaming-first responses (we accept slightly higher tail for full long outputs).

Can you confirm recommended dedicated GPU pool size (and any assumptions about quantization/model variant) and a ballpark monthly commit we should expect? Also let us know if burst overlay is supported for short peaks.

Thanks — would like a proposal we can share with procurement next week.

Best,
Alice
Head of ML Ops
Starlit AI

Attachment: starlit_workload_snapshot.csv

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@starlit-ai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-31T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask — production traffic profile + SLA goals

Hi Alice — appreciate the clear summary and the CSV. Quick read-through below and looping in Lauren for sizing nuances and Sean for commit/pricing. 

High level (rough): using your peak numbers (20 req/s) and avg tokens per request (~450 tokens total including input+output) we estimate ~9k tokens/sec at peak. On our optimized inference runtime (fp16 baseline, with optional 4-bit quantization) an A100-class serving worker yields on the order of ~1.4k–1.8k effective tokens/sec for this generation profile depending on context length and attention cost. That points to ~5–7 GPUs to cover sustained peak without excess queuing. 

Questions that will materially change this:
- How often do you hit the 4k-context path vs 1k? (the 4k path increases per-token compute 20–40% depending on model)
- How tolerant is the app to a few hundred ms tail during the 90th–99th pct long outputs?
- Are you open to enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (saves tokens for multi-step dialogs)?

Initial packaging thought: guarantee 6 GPUs reserved (monthly commit) + 2 GPUs as burst (on-demand / burst overlay) to handle the 45-minute peaks. We can propose a discount on the committed commit and offer a 10% onboarding credit on first month to offset migration/testing. Lauren — can you add a short calc and an alternative lower-commit option if Starlit invests in caching/4-bit quantization? Sean — can you draft pricing tiers for 6 vs 8 GPU commits and burst terms?

Alice — if that direction sounds reasonable I can send a formal term sheet by early next week.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Alice Moreno <alice@starlit-ai.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask — production traffic profile + SLA goals

Hi all — adding an explicit breakdown so procurement has something they can compare. I kept model assumptions conservative (fp16 runtime) and also included an optimized path if Starlit is willing to quantize and enable prefix caching.

Workload math (peak):
- Peak QPS: 20 req/s
- Avg tokens per req: input 200 + output 250 = 450 tokens
- Peak tokens/sec = 20 * 450 = 9,000 tokens/sec

Serving throughput assumptions (per GPU):
- fp16 baseline (no quant): ~1,500 tokens/sec per GPU (varies with context length; longer context decreases throughput by ~15–25%)
- 4-bit quantized + KV cache active: ~2,000 tokens/sec effective per GPU (savings variable)

Recommended sizing (sustained coverage):
- Conservative (fp16 baseline, few caching benefits): ceil(9000 / 1500) = 6 GPUs -> add 1 GPU buffer => 7 GPUs
- Optimized (quant + caching enabled): ceil(9000 / 2000) = 5 GPUs -> add 1 GPU buffer => 6 GPUs

Burst handling:
- Because you have short 45-minute peaks, we recommend a small burst overlay of 2 GPUs (on-demand) to absorb short-term overshoot without increasing committed spend.

Latency note:
- With the above sizing we expect median streaming-first tokens under 150–220ms; 95th pct for long outputs may approach 300–450ms depending on request size and cache hit rate. If 95th pct < 300ms is a hard SLA for long outputs, we'd push to the higher commit (8 GPUs) or require heavy caching/quantization.

Packaging options to propose: 
A) 6 GPU commit + 2 GPU burst (recommended if Starlit will implement KV caching + 4-bit quant)
B) 7 GPU commit + 2 GPU burst (balanced, fp16 baseline)
C) 8 GPU commit with higher discount and SLA credits (for strict latency guarantees)

I can attach a short CSV with the per-job throughput curves; Camila/Sean — let me know if you want that in the term sheet.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice@starlit-ai.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask — production traffic profile + SLA goals

Alice — thanks for the details. Camila/Lauren, good notes. Pricing sketch (ballpark) below — final numbers subject to MRC commitment and term length. I attached a draft term sheet (proposed_commit_term_sheet.pdf) you can share with procurement.

Pricing tiers (monthly committed GPUs, net of standard platform fees):
- 6 GPU commit: list $48k/mo -> with 18% commit discount -> ~$39,360/mo
- 7 GPU commit: list $56k/mo -> with 22% commit discount -> ~$43,680/mo
- 8 GPU commit: list $64k/mo -> with 26% commit discount -> ~$47,360/mo

Burst overlay: additional on-demand GPUs billed at hourly on-demand rate (we keep a soft pool for short windows).

Commercial levers we can offer:
- 10% onboarding credit (applied to first month of committed spend)
- One-time migration assistance credit (engineering time) for larger commits over 6 GPUs
- SLA credits tied to 99.9% uptime and targeted latency SLOs; strict latency SLOs (95th <300ms for long outputs) map to the 8-GPU commit or additional monitoring/optimization fees.

If Starlit prefers to start conservatively and ramp, we can structure a 6-month ramp with step-up credits so you get a higher discount once you hit the 8-GPU effective usage threshold.

Next steps I propose:
1) Starlit confirms target commit & whether caching/quantization will be enabled.
2) We send a formal term sheet + SLA appendix (attached).
3) Procurement/Legal review + PO.

Attached: proposed_commit_term_sheet.pdf

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales — Enterprise
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_commit_term_sheet.pdf

Subject: Re: Sizing ask — production traffic profile + SLA goals

Camila/Sean/Lauren — this all looks good. Procurement reviewed and we want to proceed with option B (7 GPU commit + 2 GPU burst overlay) to start — we want a little extra headroom while we enable caching and test quantization. Please send the term sheet and PO instructions; we will sign a 12-month commit if the onboarding credit and migration assistance are included.

Next steps for Redwood: send final term sheet + instructions for PO. For our part, we will schedule a short baseline runbook session with your solutions team next week (I'll share available times).

Best,
